subject: Consent scope & derivative rights — sprint plan and proposed DPA language
body_summary: Customer asked for clarity on derivative rights, training opt-ins, and subprocessor residency. Internal sprint plan includes proposed DPA redline, routing/onsite KMS options, and an evidence packet for residency/subprocessor access.
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@healthops.com>
Cc: legal@healthops.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Consent scope & derivative rights — sprint plan and proposed DPA language

Hi Samantha,

Thanks again for the call today — really appreciate you walking through the HealthOps requirements. Quick follow-up with a pragmatic plan so we can get you the contractual language and evidence you need for the procurement team. High-level asks we heard: whether HealthOps data can be used to improve models ("derivative / training"), whether prompt/response content is treated as customer property, and proof of where subprocessors process or store customer content.

Proposed next steps (attached: draft redlines + dataflow diagram):
- I’ll share a short redline to the DPA that includes an opt-in for model improvement (default: off) and an explicit statement that HealthOps retains ownership of prompt/response content.
- Karthik / Neha will prepare an evidence packet showing subprocessor residency and our onshore KMS routing options.
- If this looks workable, we’ll target a legal review by end of week and a procurement sign-off next Tuesday.

Can you confirm: 1) whether HealthOps needs a permanent "no-derivative" clause (no-training ever) vs. a temporary opt-out during pilot; and 2) if export controls/residency require a hard EU-onshore-only route for EU customers?

Attached: proposed_dpa_redlines_v3.docx (redlines + short rationale), dataflow_map_healthops.png (annotated routing).

Thanks — will assemble the sprint card and loop in Karthik/Neha.

Cheers,
David Kim
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--Attachment: proposed_dpa_redlines_v3.docx (docx, 72KB)
--Attachment: dataflow_map_healthops.png (png, 420KB)

From: Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@healthops.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthOps Legal <legal@healthops.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Consent scope & derivative rights — sprint plan and proposed DPA language

David — thanks for the note and the attachments. A few clarifying points from Legal before we progress:

1) Our default preference is a permanent prohibition on training on customer content for the production tenant (no-derivative clause). For pilot data we could consider a time-boxed opt-in, but procurement prefers the strongest language for production.
2) We need explicit language that prompt/response pairs are the property of HealthOps and cannot be retained for model improvement unless HealthOps expressly opts-in per tenant.
3) Subprocessor residency: we need documented proof that any subprocessor with access to raw prompts is located within the US for our US customers and within the EU for our EU tenant data. If Redwood relies on a cloud provider subprocessor (e.g., compute in GCP/AWS), we need a mapping of which providers and regions are used and evidence (SLA/attestation) that the data will not leave the stated region.

Can you have your legal/ops team provide a concrete redline that addresses 1–3 and the evidence packet referenced? Procurement will not move forward without that.

Samantha Nguyen
Head of Product Ops
HealthOps Systems

> On Sun, Jun 20, 2027 at 3:02 PM David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> > [original message and attachments]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Consent scope & derivative rights — sprint plan and proposed DPA language

Folks — forwarding Samantha's note. Draft language and operational notes below for David to send back. I kept the redline narrowly scoped so it’s practical for procurement while satisfying legal.

Draft DPA snippets (suggested):
- "Customer Data and Derivative Works: Customer Data (including prompts and response pairs) shall remain the exclusive property of Customer. Redwood shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or improve any models used for customer-facing inference unless Customer provides a separate, written opt-in for model improvement for the specific tenant and period indicated."

- "Subprocessor residency & access: Redwood shall ensure that subprocessors with potential access to raw request/response content process such content only within the geographic region designated by Customer (e.g., US or EU). Redwood will provide a list of subprocessors and for each a residency statement and attestations (SaaS: regions, compute providers, and any third-party managed services)."

Operational controls to support the snippets:
- Routing policy: per-tenant routing to onshore pools (US/EU) and fallback plan to encrypted, onshore KMS.
- KV/prefix caching: ensure ephemeral-only caching for tenant-marked "no-derivative" tenants; background retention policy to purge caches within X hours (default 72hrs for pilot, configurable).
- Evidence pack: create artifacts — subprocessor roster, region-specific compute manifests, signed attestations from cloud providers (where available), and a short runbook describing how we effect the opt-in/out at tenant scale.

I’ll put a minimal redline into the proposed_dpa_redlines_v3.docx and add a new annex for evidence artifacts. Neha: can you scope the evidence packet and confirm what we can deliver within 48–72 hours? Laura: can you confirm the shortest timeline for legal to approve the redline at the account level?

Karthik
Sr. Applied ML / Product Privacy
Redwood Inference

> On Tue, Jun 22, 2027 at 9:18 AM Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@healthops.com> wrote:

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@healthops.com>
Cc: HealthOps Legal <legal@healthops.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Consent scope & derivative rights — sprint plan and proposed DPA language

Samantha — thanks for the clear asks. Per Karthik/Neha/Laura’s input, attached is a concise redline plus an evidence annex we can share with procurement. Highlights: 

- Strong no-training baseline: production tenant behavior = no-training (explicit clause). Pilot data can be separately opted-in with tenant-scoped consent and a defined timebox.
- Ownership: explicit sentence that prompt/response content and any derived logs are Customer property; Redwood will not assert ownership or create derivative IP without opt-in.
- Subprocessor residency: we list subprocessors and their primary processing regions; for compute we mark primary cloud provider regions and provide an attestation summary. Where onshore KMS is requested, we can route keys and processing to US-only pools (or EU-only pools for EU tenants) and include this routing as a committed operational control in the annex.

Attachments: proposed_dpa_redlines_v3.docx (updated v3.1) and dataflow_map_healthops.png (annotated with routing and onshore-KMS options).

Next steps: please confirm if HealthOps/legal can accept the redline as marked or whether you prefer we put these terms into a standalone addendum. If acceptable, we’ll target final signatures next Wednesday and will deliver the evidence packet in parallel (Neha will share the artifacts link within 48 hours).

Appreciate the fast turnaround — happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through the redline.

Best,
David Kim
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
